title: First cohomology classifies torsors
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme (for instance a curve $C$ as in
[def-sc-curves]) and $G$ a sheaf of
abelian groups on $X_{\Et}$. There is a canonical bijection

$$
H^1(X_{\Et},G)\cong\{\text{isomorphism classes of }G\text{-torsors}\}
$$

(torsors as in [def-sc-gm-torsor]), under which the group law of
$H^1$ corresponds to the contracted product
$(T,T')\mapsto T\wedge T':=(T\times T')/G$ (antidiagonal action) and
$0$ to the trivial torsor $G$. The same holds, with the same proof,
for an abelian sheaf on the Zariski site $X_{\mathrm{Zar}}$. \emph{The bijection, named (part of the statement).} The bijection is the one of Stacks Cohomology on Sites, Lemma 03AJ (torsors and $H^1$; torsors defined in 03AH): a $G$-torsor $T$ is sent to $\delta_T(1)\in H^1(X_{\Et},G)$, the image of $1\in H^0(X_{\Et},\mathbf Z)$ under the connecting map of the short exact sequence $0\to G\to E_T\to\mathbf Z\to0$, where $E_T$ is the quotient of the free abelian sheaf $\mathbf Z[T]$ on $T$ by the relations $[g\cdot t]=[t]+g$ ($g$ a local section of $G$, $t$ of $T$) and $E_T\to\mathbf Z$ sends $[t]\mapsto1$; equivalently, on a covering trivializing $T$, $T$ corresponds to the \v{C}ech $1$-cocycle of its transition sections, whose class in $H^1$ is the same element.

proof.text:
By homological algebra,

$$
H^1(X_{\Et},G)=\operatorname{Ext}^1_{\mathrm{Ab}(X_{\Et})}(\mathbf Z_X,G):
$$

the functor $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Ab}(X_{\Et})}(\mathbf Z_X,-)$ is canonically isomorphic to the global sections functor
$\Gamma(X_{\Et},-)$ (a homomorphism $\mathbf Z_X\to F$ is
determined by the image of $1$), so the first right derived
functor of this functor is $H^1(X_{\Et},-)$ on the one hand and
$\operatorname{Ext}^1(\mathbf Z_X,-)$ on the other. By
[lem-sc-ext-torsor], $\operatorname{Ext}^1(\mathbf Z_X,G)$ is
canonically the set of isomorphism classes of $G$-torsors, and the
group structures match: the Baer sum of two extensions $E,E'$ is
the subquotient $\{(e,e'):\pi(e)=\pi'(e')\}/\{(g,-g)\}$ of
$E\times E'$, and its preimage of $1$ is
$(\pi^{-1}(1)\times\pi'^{-1}(1))/G$, the contracted product of the
two torsors; the split extension $G\oplus\mathbf Z_X$ gives the
trivial torsor. Nothing in this argument (nor in
[lem-sc-ext-torsor]) uses more than that $\mathrm{Ab}(X_{\Et})$ is the
category of abelian sheaves on a site, so it applies verbatim to
$X_{\mathrm{Zar}}$.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site with a terminal object (for instance the
small etale site $X_{\Et}$ or the Zariski site $X_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ of a
scheme $X$, e.g. of a curve $C$ as in [def-sc-curves]) and let $G$ be a
sheaf of abelian groups on $\mathcal C$, with $G$-torsors defined as in
[def-sc-gm-torsor]. Write $\mathbf Z$ for the constant sheaf. There is
a canonical bijection

$$
H^1(\mathcal C,G)=\operatorname{Ext}^1_{\mathrm{Ab}(\mathcal C)}(\mathbf Z,G)
\cong\{\text{isomorphism classes of }G\text{-torsors}\},
\qquad T\longmapsto[T],
$$

with the following properties.

- **(a)** A torsor $T$ has class $[T]=0$ if and only if it has a
  global section, i.e. if and only if it is isomorphic to the trivial
  torsor $G$.
- **(b)** The group law of $H^1$ is the contracted product: if
  $T,T',T''$ are $G$-torsors and $\mu:T\times T'\to T''$ is a morphism
  of sheaves of sets with
  $\mu(g\cdot t,t')=g\cdot\mu(t,t')=\mu(t,g\cdot t')$, then
  $[T'']=[T]+[T']$. (For example $T''=T\wedge T':=(T\times T')/G$, the
  quotient by the antidiagonal action.)

proof.text:
*Step 1: $H^1=\operatorname{Ext}^1$.* The functor
$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Ab}(\mathcal C)}(\mathbf Z,-)$ is
canonically isomorphic to the global sections functor (a homomorphism
$\mathbf Z\to F$ is determined by the image of $1$, a section over the
terminal object), so its first right derived functor is
$H^1(\mathcal C,-)$ on the one hand and
$\operatorname{Ext}^1(\mathbf Z,-)$ on the other.

*Step 2: extensions and torsors.* Given an extension
$0\to G\xrightarrow{\iota}E\xrightarrow{\pi}\mathbf Z\to0$, the
preimage $T:=\pi^{-1}(1)\subseteq E$ of the section $1$ is a
$G$-torsor: the $G$-action $g\cdot t=\iota(g)+t$ is free and
transitive on sections, $T$ has sections locally because $\pi$ is an
epimorphism of sheaves, and a section $t\in T(U)$ trivializes
$T|_U\xrightarrow{\sim}G|_U$ via $g\mapsto\iota(g)+t$.

Conversely, given a $G$-torsor $T$, define an abelian sheaf
$E:=\coprod_{n\in\mathbf Z}T^{\otimes n}$, where for $n\geq1$,
$T^{\otimes n}$ is the $n$-fold contracted product
$(T\times\cdots\times T)/G$ (quotient by the antidiagonal actions of
$G$ on pairs of factors), $T^{\otimes0}:=G$, and $T^{\otimes(-n)}$ is
the $n$-fold contracted product of the inverse torsor $T^{-1}$ (the
sheaf $T$ with $G$ acting through negation). The group law is the
concatenation $T^{\otimes m}\times T^{\otimes n}\to T^{\otimes(m+n)}$;
associativity is that of contracted products, and the inverse is given
componentwise by $T^{\otimes n}\cong(T^{-1})^{\otimes n}$. The map
$\pi:E\to\mathbf Z$ sending $T^{\otimes n}$ to $n$ is a homomorphism,
an epimorphism because each $T^{\otimes n}$ is a torsor and so has
sections locally, and its kernel is $T^{\otimes0}=G$; thus
$0\to G\to E\xrightarrow{\pi}\mathbf Z\to0$ is exact. The two
constructions are mutually inverse: for the extension built from $T$,
the preimage of $1$ is $T^{\otimes1}=T$; and for the torsor
$T:=\pi^{-1}(1)$ of an extension $E$, the addition of $E$ induces
isomorphisms $\pi^{-1}(n)\xrightarrow{\sim}T^{\otimes n}$, which
identify $E$ with $\coprod_nT^{\otimes n}$. With Step 1 this gives the
bijection $T\mapsto[T]$.

*Step 3: (a).* The trivial torsor $G$ corresponds to the split
extension $G\oplus\mathbf Z$, i.e. to the class $0$. Conversely, if the
extension $E$ of $T$ splits, a splitting $s:\mathbf Z\to E$ gives a
global section $s(1)$ of $\pi^{-1}(1)=T$. A torsor with a global
section $t$ is isomorphic to $G$ via $g\mapsto g\cdot t$.

*Step 4: (b).* The Baer sum of two extensions $E,E'$ is the
subquotient $\{(e,e'):\pi(e)=\pi'(e')\}/\{(g,-g)\}$ of $E\times E'$,
and its preimage of $1$ is $(\pi^{-1}(1)\times\pi'^{-1}(1))/G$, the
contracted product $T\wedge T'$ of the two torsors; so
$[T\wedge T']=[T]+[T']$. A morphism $\mu:T\times T'\to T''$ which is
equivariant in each argument is invariant under the antidiagonal
action, hence factors through a $G$-equivariant morphism
$T\wedge T'\to T''$ of $G$-torsors. An equivariant morphism of torsors
is an isomorphism (check locally, where it is a translation of $G$),
so $[T'']=[T\wedge T']=[T]+[T']$.
